correctness.rationale: Exact exponential hat weights certify fine optimum via all vanishing scores and global strict convexity; slopes 3,0,-1/4,-1/2 show strict concavity. For coarse family 24th-degree Taylor rational integral enclosures bound score norm by 2e-6. Centered Lebesgue Gram minors 27/80,457/7200,257/108000 prove Hessian > I/400 in radius-1/100 ball. Convexity proves unique unconstrained coarse optimum therein; jump 588249/2500000 minus 0.04 >0.195. These conditions are checked using packaged code and analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Direct explicit counterexample to the unresolved fixed-weight coarser-subdivision concavity question in the original full-text paper. Comparison with the broader regular-subdivision realizability theorem shows it neither implies nor subsumes the counterexample: it varies sample weights and studies valid concave optima. Six completed published-finding corpus semantic searches and targeted publication searches found no claim proving the exact reverse or encompassing this failure. The later correction's complete text was not available; originality is best-knowledge, not exhaustive.

value.rationale: This answers the paper's explicitly identified open coarsening question: a strictly log-concave MLE can yield a nonconcave unrestricted fit upon deleting a knot, so coarsening is not a valid general shape-preserving heuristic. Fixed-weight nonasymptotic exact counterexample is significant independently of computing an arbitrary invariant.
